questions.prompt: What does the abbreviation MAN stand for in networking?

questions.prompt: Which network type is usually limited to a few metres around one person?

expected_answer.value: LAN

questions.prompt: A company has offices in Mumbai and London joined over leased lines. Which statement is TRUE about this network?

It is a PAN because it is private

questions.prompt: Which statement about a LAN is TRUE?

expected_answer.value: It is typically owned and managed by a single organisation

options: It always needs a satellite link
It must cover at least one city

It can only contain wireless devices

questions.prompt: Which pair correctly matches a network type with a typical example?

expected_answer.value: WAN - the Internet

options: LAN - a network across several states

options: A LAN covers a larger area than a WAN
A LAN always needs the Internet, a WAN does not
A WAN covers a much larger area than a LAN
questions.explanation: The main difference is geographical coverage: WANs cover wide regions, LANs a limited local area.

questions.prompt: Which of these is an example of a PAN?

expected_answer.value: A laptop sharing a file with a nearby phone over Bluetooth

options: Computers in an office floor connected by Ethernet
Branches of a bank connected across India
A laptop sharing a file with a nearby phone over Bluetooth
Cable network covering an entire city

questions.prompt: Which statement about the Internet is FALSE?

expected_answer.value: It is owned and controlled by a single company

options: It is owned and controlled by a single company
It lets devices on different LANs communicate

expected_answer.value: PAN

questions.prompt: A university links its three campuses in different cities of one state. The connection between them is usually classified as a:

expected_answer.value: The LAN becomes part of the larger network of networks

The LAN becomes part of the larger network of networks
The LAN is no longer able to share local printers
The LAN loses its own addressing

questions.prompt: Which network type typically offers the highest data transfer speed within its own range, being short and privately owned?

expected_answer.value: LAN

questions.prompt: The full form of WAN is:

expected_answer.value: Wide Area Network

questions.explanation: WAN stands for Wide Area Network.

questions.prompt: The full form of LAN is:

expected_answer.value: Local Area Network

questions.explanation: LAN stands for Local Area Network.

questions.prompt: A wireless network connects devices only inside one apartment. Which statement is most accurate?

options: It is a WAN because it is wireless
It is a WLAN, which is a kind of LAN
It is a MAN because several devices share it

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a valid reason to call a network a WAN?

expected_answer.value: The network is owned by a large company

options: It links offices in different countries
The network is owned by a large company
It uses public telecom lines to cover long distances
It spans a very large geographical region

questions.prompt: Which network is MOST likely to use a public service such as telephone or satellite links for long-distance connection?

expected_answer.value: WAN

questions.explanation: WANs span long distances, so they commonly rely on telecom carriers and satellite links.

questions.prompt: A student argues: 'My home Wi-Fi router connects to the Internet, so my home network is a WAN.' What is the best correction?

questions.prompt: Ten offices of a firm in one city are each LANs. Joining them over a city-wide high-speed backbone produces a network classified as a:

expected_answer.value: MAN

questions.explanation: Multiple LANs linked across one city form a Metropolitan Area Network.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly compares PAN and LAN?

expected_answer.value: A PAN centres on one person's devices, while a LAN serves a building or campus

options: A PAN is bigger than a LAN
A PAN centres on one person's devices, while a LAN serves a building or campus
A LAN is limited to two devices
questions.explanation: PAN is personal-scale and a few metres; LAN spans a room, building or campus.

questions.prompt: Which device connects a computer to a wired network by providing the network interface in the computer?

expected_answer.value: Network Interface Card (NIC)

questions.explanation: The NIC is the hardware inside a computer that lets it connect to a network.

questions.prompt: Which device joins several computers in a LAN and sends data only to the intended computer?

expected_answer.value: Switch

questions.prompt: Which device broadcasts incoming data to ALL connected ports?

expected_answer.value: Hub

questions.explanation: A hub does not filter; it copies incoming data to every other port.

questions.prompt: A Wi-Fi access point mainly allows:

expected_answer.value: Wireless devices to connect to a wired network

options: Domain names to be converted to IP addresses
Digital signals to be encrypted on paper
Wireless devices to connect to a wired network
Two LANs to be merged without any address

questions.prompt: Which device chooses the best path for a data packet to reach another network?

expected_answer.value: Router

questions.explanation: Routers look at destination addresses and decide the path between networks.

questions.prompt: The word 'modem' comes from combining which two processes?

expected_answer.value: Modulation and demodulation

questions.prompt: Which device would you use to extend a network cable run that is too long and causes the signal to fade?

expected_answer.value: Repeater

questions.prompt: A hub and a switch both connect many computers in a LAN. Which statement is TRUE?

expected_answer.value: A switch sends data only to the destination port, a hub sends it to all ports

options: A hub is smarter than a switch
A hub sends data only to the destination port
A switch sends data only to the destination port, a hub sends it to all ports
Both devices route data between different networks

questions.prompt: Which device is generally used to link two networks that use different protocols or architectures?

expected_answer.value: Gateway

questions.explanation: A gateway translates between different network protocols so that dissimilar networks can communicate.

questions.prompt: Home Internet using a telephone line (DSL) needs a device that converts signals between the phone line and the computer. This device is a:

expected_answer.value: Modem

questions.explanation: A modem converts between digital data and the analog signals used on a phone line.

questions.prompt: Which statement about a router is TRUE?

expected_answer.value: It forwards packets between different networks

options: It only repeats signals without reading addresses
It forwards packets between different networks
It stores web pages for later
It converts domain names into IP addresses
questions.explanation: Routers connect networks and forward packets using IP addresses.

questions.prompt: A network has 8 computers connected through a hub. Computer 1 sends a file to Computer 2. Which computers receive the data frame at their ports?

expected_answer.value: All the other 7 computers

questions.prompt: Which device operates as the entrance point of a network, connecting a home LAN to the Internet service provider?

expected_answer.value: Router

questions.explanation: The home router connects the local network to the ISP and shares the Internet connection.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a bridge in a network?

expected_answer.value: To connect two LAN segments and filter traffic between them

options: To convert digital data to analog
To boost the signal in a long cable
To connect two LAN segments and filter traffic between them
questions.explanation: A bridge links two segments of a network and passes only the necessary traffic between them.

questions.prompt: Every NIC has a unique hardware address. It is called the:

expected_answer.value: MAC address

questions.explanation: A MAC address is the unique physical address burned into a NIC.

questions.prompt: Which statement about a repeater is FALSE?

expected_answer.value: It chooses the best route between networks

options: It chooses the best route between networks
It extends the distance a signal can travel
It works with the signal rather than deciding routes
questions.explanation: Choosing routes is the router's work; a repeater only regenerates and retransmits the signal.

questions.prompt: Match the device to its function: 'Converts between analog signals and digital data'.

expected_answer.value: Modem

questions.explanation: The modem handles modulation and demodulation for analog lines.

questions.prompt: A school wants to give wireless access to students in a hall that already has a wired LAN. Which single device should be added?

expected_answer.value: Wireless access point

questions.explanation: An access point attaches to the wired network and broadcasts Wi-Fi to wireless devices.

questions.prompt: Which device works with logical (IP) addresses to forward packets, rather than just physical (MAC) addresses?

expected_answer.value: Router

questions.explanation: Routers use IP addresses to deliver packets across networks; hubs and repeaters do not read addresses.

questions.prompt: Why is a switch generally preferred over a hub in a busy LAN?

expected_answer.value: It reduces unnecessary traffic by sending frames only to the target port

options: It makes the cable length unlimited
It converts domain names into IP addresses
It reduces unnecessary traffic by sending frames only to the target port
It allows the LAN to work without cables
questions.explanation: Selective forwarding reduces collisions and wasted traffic compared with a hub's broadcast approach.

questions.prompt: An office has two networks that use completely different protocol suites and must exchange data. Which device is the best fit?

expected_answer.value: Gateway

questions.explanation: Only a gateway can perform protocol translation between dissimilar networks.

questions.prompt: A long cable between two buildings carries a signal that becomes too weak to read at the other end. Adding a hub in the middle:

expected_answer.value: Would not be the standard solution; a repeater is designed to regenerate the signal

options: Would not be the standard solution; a repeater is designed to regenerate the signal
Is the best solution since hubs filter noise
Will convert it into an IP address
questions.explanation: Repeaters are made for signal regeneration, which is the correct fix for attenuation over distance.

questions.prompt: Which device is the 'network card' in a computer commonly called?

expected_answer.value: NIC

questions.explanation: NIC stands for Network Interface Card.

questions.prompt: Which sequence shows data flowing from a home laptop to the Internet over a DSL phone line?

expected_answer.value: Laptop, router/switch, modem, phone line, ISP

options: Laptop, router/switch, modem, phone line, ISP
Modem, laptop, phone line, router, ISP
Laptop, phone line, router, modem, ISP

questions.prompt: A student says: 'A router and a switch do the same job.' Which reply is most accurate?

expected_answer.value: A switch connects devices within a network; a router connects different networks

options: A router connects devices within one LAN; a switch connects the Internet
Both convert domain names to IP addresses
A switch connects devices within a network; a router connects different networks
questions.explanation: Switches operate inside a network; routers link separate networks and decide paths.

questions.prompt: Which device combination lets a company share one Internet connection among all its LAN computers wired in a star shape?

expected_answer.value: Modem or router with a switch

options: Two repeaters and a hub only
Modem or router with a switch
A bridge alone with no external link
questions.explanation: The modem/router provides the Internet link and the switch distributes the connection to every wired device.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a function of a hub?

expected_answer.value: Connecting multiple devices in a LAN by sharing the same signal to all ports

options: Choosing the best route for packets
Connecting multiple devices in a LAN by sharing the same signal to all ports
questions.explanation: A hub is a simple multiport repeater that sends data to all connected devices.

questions.prompt: In which topology are all devices connected to a central device such as a switch or hub?

expected_answer.value: Star topology

questions.explanation: A star topology has every node linked to a central device.

questions.prompt: Which topology connects devices in a closed loop where each device has exactly two neighbours?

expected_answer.value: Ring topology

questions.prompt: The term 'topology' in networking refers to:

expected_answer.value: The arrangement or layout of devices in a network

options: The speed of the Internet connection
The arrangement or layout of devices in a network
questions.explanation: Topology describes how nodes and links are arranged.

questions.prompt: Which topology needs the LEAST amount of cable for a small number of computers?

expected_answer.value: Bus topology

options: Ring topology only with two cables each
questions.explanation: A bus uses a single backbone cable shared by all devices, so it needs little cabling.

questions.prompt: What is the main disadvantage of a star topology?

expected_answer.value: If the central device fails, the whole network stops

options: If the central device fails, the whole network stops
Any single cable break stops the network
questions.explanation: The central hub or switch is a single point of failure.

questions.prompt: In a bus topology, what is the cable that all devices share called?

expected_answer.value: Backbone

questions.explanation: The main shared cable in a bus network is the backbone.

questions.prompt: Which topology is the easiest to expand by simply plugging a new device into the central switch?

expected_answer.value: Star topology

questions.explanation: New nodes in a star just need a cable to a free port on the central device.

questions.prompt: A mesh network of 4 fully connected computers requires how many direct links?
questions.explanation: For n nodes in a full mesh the links are n(n-1)/2 = 4*3/2 = 6.

questions.prompt: A full mesh of 5 devices needs how many direct cable links?
Which topology offers the highest reliability because there are many alternate paths?

expected_answer.value: Mesh topology

questions.explanation: In a mesh each device has multiple routes, so one failed link does not isolate it.

questions.prompt: What is the main drawback of a mesh topology?

expected_answer.value: It needs many cables and connections, so it is costly

options: It cannot connect more than two devices
It always needs a central hub
It needs many cables and connections, so it is costly
questions.explanation: Number of links grows rapidly with devices, making a mesh expensive to install.

questions.prompt: In a basic bus topology, what happens if the main backbone cable breaks?

expected_answer.value: The network is split or stops working

options: The network is split or stops working
Nothing, since data uses a hub
questions.explanation: All devices depend on the single backbone, so a break disrupts the network.

questions.prompt: A tree topology is best described as:

options: A combination of star networks connected through a bus-like backbone
Every device connected to every other device
Devices connected in a closed circle
Two computers connected by one cable

expected_answer.value: Star topology

questions.explanation: Switched Ethernet star layouts are standard because they are easy to manage.

questions.prompt: In a ring topology where data flows in one direction, what happens if one device or link fails?

expected_answer.value: Data flow can be interrupted for the whole ring

options: The central hub reroutes the data
Data flow can be interrupted for the whole ring
questions.explanation: Because data passes through each node in turn, a break can stop the ring unless it has a backup path.

questions.prompt: Which statement is TRUE about a star topology?

expected_answer.value: Faults are easy to locate because each device has its own cable to the centre

options: It uses a single shared cable
Faults are easy to locate because each device has its own cable to the centre
Cable cost is the lowest of all topologies
questions.explanation: Each node has its own link, so a faulty cable affects only that node and is simple to identify.

questions.prompt: A small lab with 6 computers connected to one switch uses which topology?

expected_answer.value: Star topology

questions.explanation: All devices connect to a central switch.

expected_answer.value: Bus topology

questions.prompt: A school wants a network where one broken cable should affect only one computer, and new computers can be added easily. Best choice?

expected_answer.value: Star topology

questions.explanation: Star isolates faults to a single cable and is simple to extend.

questions.prompt: A power company needs a control network that must keep working even if several links fail. Which topology is the best fit despite higher cost?

expected_answer.value: Mesh topology

questions.explanation: Redundant paths in a mesh keep communication alive when links fail.

questions.prompt: Which pair is correctly matched?

expected_answer.value: Bus - shared backbone; Star - central switch

options: Bus - shared backbone; Star - central switch
Bus - central switch; Star - shared backbone
Ring - central switch; Mesh - closed loop
Mesh - single cable; Ring - shared backbone
questions.explanation: Bus uses a common backbone; star uses a central connecting device.

questions.prompt: Number of direct links in a full mesh of 8 devices is:

questions.explanation: Each computer needs one cable to the switch, so 10 cables.

questions.prompt: If the central switch of a star network fails, then:

expected_answer.value: All computers lose connection with each other

Only the first computer loses connection
Only the last computer loses connection
The computers continue to talk through a backbone

questions.prompt: Why does a full mesh become impractical as the number of devices grows to a large number?

expected_answer.value: The number of links grows roughly with the square of the devices

options: The number of links stays constant
The cables must be shorter than 1 metre
Only an even number of devices is allowed

questions.prompt: Which feature makes tree topology useful for a large organisation with departments?

options: It needs no cables between departments
It connects every device to every other device
It groups star networks hierarchically so each department can be managed separately

questions.explanation: A tree extends star groups through a hierarchy, though the upper links remain critical.

questions.prompt: Compare bus and star: which statement is correct?

expected_answer.value: Bus costs less cabling, but star isolates faults better

options: Star costs less cabling and bus isolates faults better
Both are equal in fault isolation
Bus has a central device, star does not
Bus costs less cabling, but star isolates faults better

questions.prompt: In a ring where every node has two links, a mesh-like improvement is to add a second ring in the opposite direction. What is the main benefit?

expected_answer.value: If one link breaks, data can travel the other way round

options: It removes the need for cables

questions.prompt: DNS stands for:

expected_answer.value: www.wikipedia.org

questions.prompt: A DNS server stores mainly a database of:

expected_answer.value: Domain names and their IP addresses

expected_answer.value: It lets users type easy names instead of numeric addresses

questions.prompt: Which of these could a user change in network settings to use a different DNS service?

expected_answer.value: DNS server address

questions.prompt: What problem would DNS most directly solve for a person who runs a new website?

expected_answer.value: Visitors can use a readable name instead of a number

options: Their site becomes immune to viruses
Their site loads without a server
Visitors can use a readable name instead of a number
questions.explanation: The domain name makes the site easy to remember and share.

questions.prompt: Which statement distinguishes a URL from a domain name?

expected_answer.value: A URL includes the protocol and path, while the domain name is only the site's name part

options: A domain name includes the protocol
A URL includes the protocol and path, while the domain name is only the site's name part
questions.explanation: For https://www.example.com/page, the domain is www.example.com; the URL has the scheme and path too.

questions.prompt: Why does the browser need DNS even though routers forward packets?

expected_answer.value: Routers need a numeric destination address, which DNS supplies from the name

options: Routers only work with MAC addresses
Routers need a numeric destination address, which DNS supplies from the name
questions.explanation: Packets are routed by IP address, so the name must first be resolved.

questions.prompt: Which sequence is more accurate for opening http://www.example.com?

expected_answer.value: Resolve name via DNS, connect to the IP, request the page

options: Request the page, resolve the name, connect
Resolve name via DNS, connect to the IP, request the page
questions.explanation: The IP address must be found first so a connection can be made before requesting a page.

questions.prompt: Which is easier for humans to remember?

expected_answer.value: A domain name

questions.explanation: Domain names exist to make addresses memorable.

questions.prompt: How many bits are used in an IPv4 address?
questions.explanation: IPv4 addresses are 32 bits long.

questions.prompt: IPv4 addresses are usually written in which format?

expected_answer.value: Four decimal numbers separated by dots

options: Eight hexadecimal groups separated by colons
Six pairs of hex digits separated by hyphens
Four decimal numbers separated by dots
questions.explanation: Dotted decimal notation such as 192.168.1.1 is used for IPv4.

questions.prompt: Which notation uses hexadecimal digits separated by colons?

expected_answer.value: IPv6

questions.explanation: IPv6 addresses are written in hexadecimal with colons, e.g. 2001:db8::1.

questions.prompt: Each of the four numbers in an IPv4 address (an octet) can range from:
questions.explanation: Each octet is 8 bits, so values run from 0 to 255.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a valid IPv4 address?
questions.explanation: 300 is greater than 255, which is not possible in an octet.

questions.prompt: How many groups of hexadecimal digits does a full IPv6 address have?
questions.explanation: A full IPv6 address has eight groups of four hex digits separated by colons.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a valid IPv6 address?
questions.explanation: Eight colon-separated groups of hexadecimal digits form a valid IPv6 address.

questions.prompt: Approximately how many addresses can IPv4 provide in theory?

expected_answer.value: About 4.3 billion

questions.explanation: 2^32 is about 4.29 billion addresses.

questions.prompt: Which statement is TRUE about IPv6 compared with IPv4?

expected_answer.value: IPv6 offers a vastly larger address space

options: IPv6 offers a vastly larger address space
IPv6 addresses are written in dotted decimal
IPv6 was designed to replace domain names
questions.explanation: IPv6 has 128-bit addresses, enough for an enormous number of devices.

questions.prompt: The double colon (::) in an IPv6 address is used to:

expected_answer.value: Replace one run of consecutive groups of zeros

options: Separate the network from the host
Mark the end of the address
Replace one run of consecutive groups of zeros
questions.explanation: One sequence of all-zero groups can be shortened to '::'.

questions.prompt: Which IPv4 address is the loopback address used to test your own computer?
questions.explanation: 127.0.0.1 refers to the local machine itself (localhost).

questions.prompt: Which of these is a private IPv4 address commonly used inside home networks?
questions.explanation: 192.168.x.x is a private range used on local networks.

questions.prompt: Each of the four parts of an IPv4 address is called an:

expected_answer.value: Octet

questions.explanation: Each part holds 8 bits and is called an octet.

questions.prompt: Which is a main reason IPv6 was created?

expected_answer.value: The shortage of IPv4 addresses

options: To make Wi-Fi faster in every case
To remove the need for routers
questions.explanation: IPv4's address space was nearly exhausted, motivating IPv6.

questions.prompt: Each group in a full IPv6 address contains how many bits?
questions.explanation: 128 bits divided into 8 groups gives 16 bits per group.

questions.prompt: How many hexadecimal digits are in each group of a full IPv6 address?
questions.explanation: Each 16-bit group is written as 4 hex digits.

questions.prompt: In IPv6, can the leading zeros in a group be left out? E.g. 0db8 written as db8.

expected_answer.value: Yes, leading zeros in a group may be omitted

options: No, all four digits must always be shown
Only if the group is the first one
Yes, leading zeros in a group may be omitted
questions.explanation: Leading zeros inside a group can be dropped, shortening the notation.

questions.prompt: Which IPv6 address is a correctly shortened form of 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0001?
questions.explanation: Leading zeros are dropped and one run of zero groups becomes '::'.

questions.prompt: Why is '2001::db8::1' NOT a valid IPv6 address?

expected_answer.value: '::' can appear only once in an address

options: It needs dots instead of colons
'::' can appear only once in an address
questions.explanation: Two '::' would make it ambiguous how many zero groups each stands for.

questions.prompt: Which statement about IPv4 and IPv6 is correct?

expected_answer.value: They are different protocol versions and are not directly compatible without special support

options: IPv6 is just IPv4 with extra dots
IPv4 can hold more devices than IPv6
They are different protocol versions and are not directly compatible without special support
questions.explanation: IPv4 and IPv6 are separate protocols; transition methods allow them to coexist.

questions.prompt: Which is a valid IPv4 address?
questions.explanation: It has four octets, each from 0 to 255.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true of IPv6 addresses?

expected_answer.value: They are 128 bits long, written in hexadecimal

options: They are 64 bits long, written in decimal
They are 128 bits long, written in hexadecimal
They are 32 bits long, written in binary only
They are 128 bits long, written in dotted decimal
questions.explanation: IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses in hexadecimal with colons.

questions.prompt: Which digit or letter is NOT allowed in an IPv6 address?

expected_answer.value: G

questions.explanation: Hexadecimal uses 0-9 and A-F only, so G is invalid.

questions.prompt: An IPv4 address is 32 bits split into 4 octets. What is the largest possible value of one octet in decimal?
questions.explanation: 8 bits can express 0 to 2^8-1 = 255.

questions.prompt: How many times larger in bit length is an IPv6 address than an IPv4 address?

expected_answer.value: 4 times

questions.explanation: IPv6 addresses are 128 bits long and IPv4 addresses 32 bits, so 128 / 32 = 4 times larger.

questions.prompt: Which IPv6 address is the loopback (like 127.0.0.1 in IPv4)?
questions.explanation: The IPv6 loopback address is 0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1, written ::1.

questions.prompt: Every device on a network may have a MAC address AND an IP address. Which is TRUE?

expected_answer.value: The MAC address is hardware-based, while the IP address is logical and can change

options: Both are assigned by the DNS
The IP address is burned into the NIC
The MAC address is always written in dotted decimal
The MAC address is hardware-based, while the IP address is logical and can change
questions.explanation: A MAC is a fixed hardware address of the NIC; IPs are assigned logically and may change with networks.

questions.prompt: A router has the address 192.168.1.1. Which part of this notation lets us call it IPv4?

expected_answer.value: It has four dot-separated decimal octets

options: It has four dot-separated decimal octets
questions.explanation: IPv4 is recognised by dotted-decimal octets.

questions.prompt: What does the 's' in HTTPS stand for?

expected_answer.value: Secure

questions.explanation: HTTPS is HTTP Secure; the data is encrypted.

questions.prompt: HTTPS is mainly used to:

expected_answer.value: Protect data sent between a browser and a website

options: Protect data sent between a browser and a website
questions.explanation: HTTPS encrypts traffic so others cannot read it easily.

questions.prompt: Which of these web addresses uses a secure connection?

expected_answer.value: https://www.example.com

questions.explanation: Only the https:// scheme uses an encrypted connection.

questions.prompt: Before entering a card number on a shopping site, you should check that the address starts with:

expected_answer.value: https://

questions.explanation: HTTPS indicates the data is encrypted in transit.

questions.prompt: Which protocol is used by HTTPS to encrypt data?

expected_answer.value: SSL/TLS

questions.explanation: HTTPS uses TLS (earlier SSL) to encrypt data between client and server.

questions.prompt: What does plain HTTP lack compared with HTTPS?

expected_answer.value: Encryption of the data in transit

options: Encryption of the data in transit
questions.explanation: HTTP sends data in readable form, so others on the network may read it.

questions.prompt: Which is a typical symbol shown by browsers for a secure HTTPS page?

expected_answer.value: A padlock icon

questions.explanation: A padlock beside the address indicates a secure connection.

questions.prompt: A website has a padlock and https. Which statement is MOST accurate?

expected_answer.value: Data between you and the site is encrypted, but the site could still be unsafe

options: The site is guaranteed to be honest
The site cannot contain any malware
Your computer is immune to viruses
Data between you and the site is encrypted, but the site could still be unsafe
questions.explanation: HTTPS protects the channel, not the site's honesty or content.

questions.prompt: What is a digital certificate used for in HTTPS?

expected_answer.value: To prove the identity of the website and enable encryption

options: To prove the identity of the website and enable encryption
questions.explanation: Certificates issued by trusted authorities verify the website's identity.

questions.prompt: Who issues digital certificates that browsers trust?

expected_answer.value: A Certificate Authority (CA)

questions.explanation: A CA verifies websites and signs their certificates.

questions.prompt: Which scenario most needs HTTPS?

expected_answer.value: Entering a password on a login page

options: Reading a public notice board page
Watching the clock on a page
Entering a password on a login page
questions.explanation: Sensitive data like passwords should always travel over encrypted connections.

questions.prompt: On public Wi-Fi, why is HTTPS valuable?

expected_answer.value: It makes it hard for others on the network to read what you send

options: It makes it hard for others on the network to read what you send
It makes the Wi-Fi password unnecessary
questions.explanation: Encryption prevents eavesdroppers on the same network from reading page data.

questions.prompt: Which of these is TRUE about HTTP?

expected_answer.value: Data is sent as plain text without encryption

options: Data is sent as plain text without encryption
questions.explanation: HTTP does not encrypt data, unlike HTTPS.

questions.prompt: A browser shows 'Not secure' next to a login form. What should the user do?

expected_answer.value: Avoid entering sensitive information on that page

options: Avoid entering sensitive information on that page
questions.explanation: Not secure means the connection is unencrypted, so passwords could be exposed.

questions.prompt: Encryption in HTTPS means:

expected_answer.value: Data is converted into a coded form that only the intended parties can read

options: Data is compressed to save space
Data is sent to many servers
Data is converted into a coded form that only the intended parties can read
questions.explanation: Encryption scrambles information using keys.

questions.prompt: The typical default port of HTTPS is:
questions.explanation: HTTPS uses port 443; HTTP uses 80.

questions.prompt: The typical default port number for plain HTTP is:
questions.explanation: HTTP normally uses port 80.

questions.prompt: A phishing page copies a bank's design and has https and a padlock. Which statement is correct?

expected_answer.value: HTTPS alone does not prove a site is genuine, so check the domain name carefully

options: The padlock proves the bank owns the site
HTTPS alone does not prove a site is genuine, so check the domain name carefully
Padlock means the page is safe for all passwords
questions.explanation: Attackers can also get certificates, so you must still verify the web address.

questions.prompt: Which security benefit is NOT provided by HTTPS alone?

expected_answer.value: Protection from malware you voluntarily download from the site

options: Protection from malware you voluntarily download from the site
Protection from eavesdropping on the connection
Verification of the site's identity by certificate
questions.explanation: HTTPS protects the transmission, not the safety of files you download.

questions.prompt: A student sees http://mybank-login.example. What is the BEST action?

expected_answer.value: Do not enter any details; the page is unencrypted and suspicious

options: Do not enter any details; the page is unencrypted and suspicious
questions.explanation: The page lacks encryption and the name looks suspicious, so avoid entering any details.

questions.prompt: Which statement about HTTP and HTTPS is correct?

expected_answer.value: HTTPS is HTTP running over an encrypted TLS connection

options: HTTPS is a different language to write web pages
HTTP is the newer secure version
HTTPS is HTTP running over an encrypted TLS connection
questions.explanation: HTTPS means the same HTTP messages are sent through TLS.

questions.prompt: If a website certificate is expired, the browser will usually:

expected_answer.value: Show a warning that the connection may not be private

options: Show a warning that the connection may not be private
Silently switch to a different site
Remove the padlock without telling the user
questions.explanation: Browsers warn users when certificates are invalid or expired.

questions.prompt: Which statement about HTTPS is FALSE?

expected_answer.value: HTTPS prevents the website from collecting your data

options: HTTPS prevents the website from collecting your data
questions.explanation: HTTPS only secures the connection; the website can still collect data you give it.

questions.prompt: Why can a certificate help prevent an attacker from impersonating a website?

expected_answer.value: A trusted CA has verified the site, so the browser can check the identity

options: A trusted CA has verified the site, so the browser can check the identity
questions.explanation: The browser checks the certificate signed by a trusted CA to confirm identity.

questions.prompt: Which situation shows the risk of using HTTP on a shared network?

expected_answer.value: Someone on the same network could read a form's text, including a password

options: Someone on the same network could read a form's text, including a password
The page loads in a different language
questions.explanation: Unencrypted traffic can be captured by others on the same network.

questions.prompt: A page loads over HTTPS but includes a form that submits to an http:// address. What is the concern?

expected_answer.value: The form data would be sent without encryption

options: Nothing, since the page has a padlock
The form will be encrypted twice
The form data would be sent without encryption
questions.explanation: What matters is where the data is submitted; an http target is not encrypted.

questions.prompt: Which is the best order for checking a site before paying online?

expected_answer.value: Check https and padlock, verify the domain name, then enter details

options: Look only at the page colours
Check https and padlock, verify the domain name, then enter details
Check only if the site has ads
questions.explanation: Verify the secure connection and site identity before sharing payment details.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a good reason to prefer HTTPS sites for online banking?

expected_answer.value: It protects login details while they travel over the network

options: It makes the bank give a higher interest
It protects login details while they travel over the network
It removes the need for passwords
questions.explanation: HTTPS encrypts the data so login details are not exposed in transit.

questions.prompt: A school wants its lab computers to share one broadband line to the Internet, with a device that also joins them to each other by Wi-Fi. Which device fits best?

expected_answer.value: Wireless router

questions.explanation: A wireless router joins devices into one network, shares the Internet connection and provides Wi-Fi.
